newsitem.title: ITALY: Alitalia losses worsen in first half.
newsitem.headline: Alitalia losses worsen in first half.

text.p: Italian flag carrier Alitalia said on Friday it plunged further into the red in the first half of 1996 as the company hurtled towards its ninth straight year of losses.

Alitalia, which in June rallied unions round a do-or-die plan to haul the group back to profit, said it made a 310 billion lire ($203.9 million) loss in the first six months of the year against 197 billion lire in the same period last year.
The firm predicted a hefty full-year loss, with some 900 billion lire being put aside for restructuring charges.
"This should allow a rapid return to the black in 1997 and a significantly improving trend in the years thereafter," the company said in a statement.
Alitalia said turnover rose to 3.77 trillion lire between January and June, up 6.1 percent on the first half in 1995, while passenger numbers rose 10.8 percent.

The company said two thirds of the additional cash was swallowed up on improvements to its fleet and money was also spent on opening new connections to China and Japan as well as additional short-haul flights within Europe.
An increase in fuel costs also hurt the balance sheet.

Alitalia said the new loss pushed its capital base back into the red. Mounting losses at the airline wiped out its equity, forcing the government to inject 905 billion lire of fresh funds into the firm at the end of March.
Some 272 billion lire of this was aimed at covering first half losses, but the fresh overshoot has now left Alitalia with negative capital of 38 billion lire.
Company debt totalled 3.34 trillion lire on June 30 leaving it with a 209 billion lire interest repayment bill.

Alitalia's parent company, state-controlled IRI, itself heavily indebted, threw the carrier a lifeline in July when it agreed to a 3.135 trillion lire recapitalisation designed to save the group from collapse.
IRI has pledged to inject 1.5 trillion lire of fresh funds under the capital increase. The remainder is due to come from the private sector next year.
The rescue plan was sealed after agreement between management and unions on cost cuts and job losses.
"The first half losses....confirm the need to start immediately with the structural changes," Alitalia said. $1 = 1.520 lire
